title: Six-round AES-128 truncated-boomerang secret-key distinguisher, multiple-trail construction

target.description: Six-round AES-128 with the initial AddRoundKey and no final MixColumns, following Figure 3 and Section 4.1. The construction permits the ordinary AES key schedule without exploiting it.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES-128 key for both forward and inverse queries.
setting.key_population: general secret AES-128 key under the paper's probabilistic trail model
setting.plaintext_model: chosen diagonal structures and adaptive ciphertext structures, with returning pairs in any single diagonal
setting.reference_model: Distinguish the six-round secret-key permutation and inverse from a uniform random 128-bit permutation and its inverse by the returning-quartet count; no subkey guess is used in the decision rule.
assumptions: The multiple-trail analysis inherits Section 3.1's independent-event and sample approximations.
Section 4.1 combines four upper trails, sixteen lower trails, and a different returning-pair set; its final parameters are p_b=2^-122, p_random=2^-94, c=4 and Q=2^152.
Adaptive inverse access is essential to the construction.

time.note: Final Section 4.1 result and Table 1 give T=2^87 under the source's oracle-call-dominated time model.

data.note: Final Section 4.1 result gives D=2^87; Table 1 labels access as ACC, meaning chosen plaintexts plus adaptively chosen ciphertexts.

memory.note: Source Eq6 applied to the final Section4.1 sets, |Din^0|=2^32 and|Dout^1|=2^34: min(2^87,2^66)=2^66 entries. Formula-derived scale; no bytes/overhead conversion.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing budget is tabulated.

success.description: Section 4.1 explicitly sets c=4 in the Section 3.1 statistical model, which gives Phi(sqrt(c)/2), approximately 0.84. This applies the source's stated decision-probability formula to its optimized parameters, not a measured full-scale experiment.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4, Table 1; pp.10-12, Section 3.1 statistical decision model; pp.17-18, Section 4.1, especially 'Different Set ... for Returning Pairs' and final T=D=2^87 (c=4).
evidence.interpretation: The final six-round distinguisher uses three cumulative multiple-trail refinements. Its success estimate follows the paper's explicitly reused formula; intermediate 2^91 and 2^89 costs are not substituted for the final result.

evidence.locator: Complete exact primary PDF1–56, all sections, formulas, tables, algorithms, appendices and references.
evidence.interpretation: Complete reading and source inventory; later-literature gates and finite controls separately recorded. No author attack code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF11 Eq6; PDF17–18 Section4.1 input/output sets for final variant.
evidence.interpretation: Complete source formula supplies the previously unextracted memory scale.

limitations: The statistical model and 2^87-scale construction have not been independently reproduced.
Later boomerang work is tracked separately; this source-version-specific record carries no current-best claim.
